title: Tomato Sauce, Rich And Very Fine
description: A sauce made with tomatoes, ham, and thyme or parsley.

ingredients.name: a bunch of thyme or parsley

steps: Pick off the stalks from the tomatoes
Extract the seeds and watery juice by squeezing them in the hand
Place the pulp in a stewpan with four ounces of raw ham, cut into cubes
Add a dozen small eschalots and a bunch of thyme or parsley
Throw in a little butter, and fry all gently until the tomatoes soften sufficiently to be passed through a strainer
Mix this puree with a cupful of good soup-stock
Add the strained juice of the tomatoes
Let boil fifteen minutes, then set it by to clarify
Serve it hot

title: Tomato Soup With Vegetables. Very Fine
description: A soup made with carrots, celery, and onions.

ingredients.name: two or three quarts of good soup stock

steps: Cut small, three carrots, three heads of celery, four onions and two turnips; put them into a saucepan with a tablespoonful of butter, a slice of ham and a half cup of water; let them simmer gently for an hour; then if a very rich soup is desired add to the vegetables two or three quarts of good soup stock, made by boiling a beef bone in three quarts of water until the meat is tender. Let all boil together for half an hour, and then add ten or twelve ripe tomatoes and a half-dozen whole peppers. It should cook for another hour or so. It must then be strained through a sieve or coarse cloth. Serve with toasted or fried bread cut in bits in the tureen. This is an elegant family soup, particularly nice in summer when the vegetables are fresh.

title: Tomato Wine
description: Prepared with tomatoes and white sugar.
steps: Let the tomatoes be very ripe

This wine will be a pleasant acid, and should be served with sugar and water, in the tumbler with the wine

title: Transparent Icing
description: Prepared with white sugar, juice, and liqueur.

ingredients.name: Half of the White of 1 Egg
The Juice of Half a Lemon

steps: Take a half pound of the finest white clarified sugar, and clarify again by boiling it with half of the white of an egg, beaten to a stiff froth
Clear off the scum as it rises, and continue skimming till the sugar is perfectly clear
Then add to the sugar half a gill of clarified sugar, boiled to a syrup, and to which you will have added the juice of a quarter or half a lemon
Strain, and add to the sugar enough Liqueur, Curaçoa, Noyau, Cedrati or Maraschino to flavor the icing to taste, and beat or whip it to the proper consistency
Then take a silver tablespoon and stir the sugar well together, rubbing up and against the sides of the pan till it acquires an opaline appearance
Then take a silver fork, lift one of the cakes intended to be iced, dip in the sugar, or else hold it on a fork and with a spoon pour the icing over
Take another fork, lift off the cake and place it on the baking sheet, and so on till all the small cakes are iced
Then dry in the sun or in the oven for about ten minutes

title: Transparent Pudding
description: A pudding made with eggs, butter, and sugar.
steps: Beat eight eggs very light
Add them to half a pound of butter, and the same of sugar, which have been beaten to a cream together
Grate in half a nutmeg
Set it on the fire in a stew-pan, and stir it constantly until it is hot
Do not leave it more than five minutes on the fire, as you only wish to slightly cook the whites of the eggs to prevent their running when put on the paste
Line two pie pans with delicate paste, and pour in the mixture
Bake in a moderate oven
Do not allow the top to burn, as it will, if not covered when first put in the oven
Cover with a pan until the bottom is cooked, and then a few moments colors the top
Serve it with a tart pie

title: Tripe a la Creole
description: Prepared with tripe, tomatoes, and onions.

ingredients.name: 3 Sprigs Each of Thyme and Bay Leaf

Chop about one inch square of lean ham very fine, and add.
Take two cloves of garlic, chopped fine, with three sprigs each of thyme and bay leaf, minced very fine, put in the saucepan, and let all brown.
Then add about twelve large, fresh tomatoes, or the contents of a two-pound can.
Season all to taste with salt and Cayenne pepper.
Let it cook for ten minutes, and then add the tripe, and let all smother for twenty-five minutes.

title: Tripe a la Mode de Caen
description: Prepared with tripe, onions, and carrots.

ingredients.name: 2 dozen pieces of bacon 2 inches square
salt, Cayenne and Chili pepper to taste

steps: Take three pounds of tripe and cut the tripe into pieces of about two inches square
Slice three onions and three large carrots very fine

Have ready a two-gallon earthen jar that can stand baking in an oven
Put in the bottom of the jar a thin layer of butter
Place on top a thin layer of bacon, then a thin layer of onions, carrots, bay leaves, thyme, garlic, spices, dividing into two equal portions the whole amount

Pour over all a half bottle of White Wine and one cup of broth or water

title: Turkey en Daube

ingredients.name: 1 Bunch Each of Parsley, Thyme and Small Celery Leaves

steps: Clean and prepare the turkey, then stuff either with egg dressing or oyster stuffing.
Rub well with salt and pepper.
Place at the bottom of a deep pot slender strips of salt pork and half of a calf's foot, well prepared.
Place on top of this the slices of onions, carrots, fine herbs, minced nicely; garlic, minced, celery, parsley, etc., and lay the turkey on this bed.
Pour over it one pint of white wine and two tablespoonfuls of brandy, and one pint and a half of good broth or boiling water.
Season well to taste and cover tightly.
Set on the stove to simmer very slowly for at least five hours if the turkey is old.
Turn it once very carefully when half done cooking.
After five hours, lift the turkey out of the sauce, place on a hot dish.
Strain the sauce through a sieve, and if the turkey is served at once, serve hot in a separate dish.
If not, pour it over the turkey and set it away to cool.

title: Turtle Soup
description: A soup made with turtle, leg of beef, and onions.

ingredients.name: 2 quarts and a half of soup

steps: Take the whole of the turtle out of the shell; cut it in pieces, that it may be more easily scalded
Throw these pieces, with the fins, into the pot, and when scalded, take off the coarse skin of the fins and lay them aside to make another dish
Take off the thick skin of the stomach; under it lies the fat, or what is termed the citron
Cut up the turtle in small pieces, throw them into a pot
Before doing this, take a leg of beef and boil it to a gravy
Put in the pieces of turtle, adding as much water as will cover the whole, about 2 inches
Let it boil slowly for 3 hours
The seasoning and the citron should be put in when the soup is half done
To 2 quarts and a half of soup add an ounce of mace, a dessertspoonful of allspice, a teaspoonful of cloves, and salt, black and cayenne pepper to your taste
Use parsley, thyme, and onions in the soup while boiling
When nearly done thicken with 2 tablespoons of flour

title: Turtle Soup for a Large Company, No. 1
description: A soup made with turtle, beef or veal, and ham or bacon.

ingredients.name: eight pounds of beef or veal
one pound of ham or bacon
pepper, salt, and sweet herbs to taste
the liquor of a boiled turtle
the flesh of the turtle, prepared as in recipe No. 1
a quarter of a pound of good sweet butter

steps: Cut the head off the turtle the day before you dress it, and drain the blood thoroughly from the body
Then cut it up in the following manner: Divide the back, belly, head and fins from the intestines and lean parts
Be careful not to cut the gall bag
Scald in boiling water to remove the skin and shell
Cut up in neat pieces and throw into cold water
Boil the back and belly in a little water long enough to extract the bones easily
If for a large company a leg of veal will also be required, and a slice of ham, which must be stewed with the lean parts till well browned
Then add boiling water, and the liquor and bones of the boiled turtle
Season with sliced lemon, whole pepper, a bunch of parsley, two leeks sliced, and salt to taste

title: Turtle Soup No. 2
description: A soup made with turtle, lard, and tomatoes.

ingredients.name: 1 Glass of Sherry or White Wine

steps: Clean the turtle and entrails by cutting open the latter and washing thoroughly in cold water.
Put the meat and entrails into a saucepan and parboil them for ten minutes. Carefully save this stock of water.
Chop the onion very fine, and cut the ham into very fine pieces.
Cut the turtle meat into one-inch pieces; mash the allspice very fine, and mince the parsley, thyme and bay leaf.
Brown the onions in the lard and butter mixed, and almost immediately add the turtle meat.
Brown together for ten minutes and add the finely chopped ham.
As this continues to brown, add the cloves of garlic minced fine, the thyme and bay leaf and the ground allspice.
Mix all together, stirring almost constantly to prevent burning.
Add the well-rubbed tablespoonfuls of flour, stirring constantly.
Scald and skin the tomatoes and chop them fine, and add to the turtle meat.

When well-browned, pour over three quarts of the water in which the turtle was parboiled, season with salt and pepper and Cayenne to taste, and let it boil slowly for fully an hour, stirring frequently.
After one hour, taste the soup, and if not sufficiently seasoned, add seasoning of salt, pepper and Cayenne again, according to taste.
Let it cook for an hour longer and then take off the stove if the turtle is thoroughly done. This may be ascertained by sticking it with a fork. If no blood exudes, the soup is ready to serve.
Take off the stove and strain through a colander into the tureen.
Add the whites and yolks of two hard-boiled eggs, chopped fine, and one good glass of Sherry or White Wine.
Slice a lemon fine and add to the soup and serve hot.

Roll the strips of salt meat, which must be about three inches in length and one-half inch thick, in this.
Make incisions into the rump of meat and force in the strips of fat meat and the spices.
Rub the whole well with salt and pepper, judging according to taste, and proceed to cook according to the recipe for Beef à la Mode.
Let the daube cook about four hours when you intend to serve it cold.
In the meantime, in another pot, place a veal steak of about two pounds and two pigs' feet.
Season well with salt and pepper and Cayenne, and cover well with four quarts of water, and let them boil.
Add one bay leaf, one sprig of thyme, one-half clove of garlic and one onion, all minced very fine, and two cloves mashed into almost a jelly, and one glass of Sherry or Madeira Wine.
Let these boil well with the veal and pigs' feet.
When the veal and pigs' feet are cooked very tender, take them out of the pot and mince the meat of each very fine.
Return to the sauce, and again season highly, according to taste.
After the daube has cooked four or five hours, take off the stove and pour over the sauce and set all in a cool place.

title: Vegetable Soup
description: A soup made with split peas, white beans, and celery.
steps: Soak all night in cold water either two quarts of yellow split peas or two quarts of dried white beans
In the morning drain them
Season them with a very little salt and cayenne and a head of minced celery, or else a heaped tablespoonful of celery seed
Put them into a soup pot with four quarts of water
Boil them slowly till they are all dissolved
Stir them frequently
Have ready a quantity of fresh vegetables, such as turnips, carrots, parsnips, potatoes, onions, also salsify, and asparagus tops
Put in first the vegetables that require the longest boiling
Cut all vegetables into small pieces
Enrich the whole with some bits of fresh butter rolled in flour
Boil these vegetables in the soup till they are quite tender
Put it in a tureen and serve it up

title: Venison Hash
description: Prepared with venison, potatoes, and lard or butter.
steps: After having taken off all the rough edges of the roast and cut out the gristle and hard membrane, hash the venison into pieces of about one-inch in size.
Take six left-over tomatoes, or freshly boiled, and cut into quarters.
Chop fine one herb bouquet.
Place a tablespoonful of butter or a half tablespoonful of lard into the stewpot, and as it melts add the venison, seasoned well, and a few minutes later the fine herbs.
Mince the clove of garlic if the flavor is liked and add.
Stir constantly without browning much, and add a tablespoonful of flour.
Let this brown very slightly, and then add the tomatoes.
Cover and let all simmer for about twenty minutes, and then pour over a pint of boiling water.
Season again to taste and set back on the stove and let it simmer gently for about three-quarters of an hour.
Cut some Croutons and fry them in butter; place on a dish and serve with the hash.

description: Prepared with venison, onion, and ham.
steps: Cut the venison into pieces of about two inches square.

Stir in with the rabbit and let these brown for about two minutes.
Then add a tablespoonful of flour and brown for a few minutes more.
Add a half bottle of White Wine and let all simmer for five minutes.
Then add a quart of consommé or water and let all cook for about one hour.
Season again according to taste and add a half can of mushrooms chopped fine and the zest of a lemon and season again to taste.

title: Vermicelli Soup, No. 2
description: A soup made with vermicelli, veal, and mutton.

ingredients.name: four pounds of knuckle of veal

one head of celery cut fine

steps: Cut about four pounds of knuckle of veal, one pound and a half of the scrag of mutton, and a few slices of ham into small pieces; put them into a saucepan with one onion stuck with cloves, and four ounces of butter; then add the carrots, mace, bunch of sweet herbs, one anchovy, and the celery. Mix all together, cover it close, and set it over the fire till all the gravy has been extracted from the meat; pour the liquor into a bowl, let the meat brown in the pan, and add to it four quarts of water; boil it slowly till it is reduced to three pints, strain it, and stir in the gravy drawn from the meat. Set it over the fire, add the vermicelli, one head of celery cut fine, a little cayenne, and salt; boil it up for ten minutes. Lay a French roll in the tureen, pour the soup over it, and strew some vermicelli on the top.

Cut around the edge nicely with a knife.

Then set it in a very hot oven to bake for about half an hour.

steps: Pour 3 liters of water over 14 dekagrams sweet almonds and 6 bitter almonds and let stand 24 hours, after which they can be easily peeled.
Alternatively, if time is short, place in hot water to peel, then place in fresh water for a while to harden and make them brittle.
Remove, dry with clean cloth, and pound to paste in mortar.
Place the ground almonds in a porcelain pan, pour 1 liter of well water over them, and stir finely with silver spoon.
Strain through cloth, pour the strained liquid back over the almonds, and strain again, pressing with greatest force until all liquid is extracted.
Beat this almond milk with 28 dekagrams finely ground sugar.
Mix in 4.5 dekagrams isinglass that has been boiled down to 5 spoonfuls.
Strain again through cloth, pour into molds, and place on ice.

title: Ananász-Kocsonya (Pineapple Aspic)
description: Prepared with pineapples, juice, and fish.

ingredients.name: one and one-quarter dekagrams dissolved fish glue

steps: Peel the two large ripe pineapples and crush the peel in a mortar
Pour eight deciliters water over it
Dissolve in a brass pan and strain
In this liquid cook thirty-five dekagrams sugar until it becomes invisible
Cut the pineapple into thin slices
Cook fourteen dekagrams sugar in two deciliters water until it begins to thicken
Place the slices into this syrup, bring to a boil for a few minutes
Set aside and let cool
Strain off the juice and mix with the already-cooked sugar
Add the juice of three lemons and one and one-quarter dekagrams dissolved fish glue
After mixing everything well, strain through a taut kitchen cloth
When the entire aspic mass is clear, pour two centimeters height into a mold that has been strongly packed in ice
Let it freeze, then arrange half of the pineapple slices on top
Pour over half a coffee cup of unfrozen juice, which must then freeze to hold the pieces in place
Pour aspic juice over it, and when it has frozen, arrange the second half of the pineapple slices on top
When these are also frozen as the first ones were, pour the final part of the aspic over it
Cover the whole with a tin plate loaded with ice and keep in the ice until, with care and speed, you turn it out onto the table

Remove the pot from the coals and when the mixture begins to boil, fold in the beaten egg whites

title: Barnaleves Rántott Borsóval (Brown Sauce with Fried Peas)
description: A sauce made with fat, flour, and eggs.
steps: Beat three eggs into four tablespoons flour in a pot.
Mix the two together well.
Slowly pour in milk until the batter is as thin as a nice smooth crepe batter.
Season lightly with salt.
Melt clear fat in a frying pan.
Drop the batter in with a foam skimmer.
Shake the pan several times so the peas brown evenly on all sides.
Add to the soup only at the moment of serving, as they should not become too soft.

title: Becsinált Jércze (Breaded Young Hen in Cream Sauce)
description: A sauce made with hen, broth, and sour cream.
steps: After cleaning and preparing the hens, blanch and slice them nicely.
Prepare the sauce as follows: melt seven dekagrams of butter, blend smoothly with two spoonfuls of flour, two spoonfuls of broth, half a spoonful of sour cream and the juice of one lemon.
The hens, which have been nearly cooked in broth beforehand, are only braised in this sauce with continuous stirring.
At the same time, shape beautiful cutlets from veal and cook their sauce until reduced.
Pile the hens high in the center of the dish and pour their sauce over them; arrange the cutlets around the edge in a wreath, poured with their own broth.

title: Becsinált Mazsolával (Poultry with Raisins)

title: Berakott burgonya (Layered Potato Casserole)
description: Prepared with potatoes, ham, and sour cream.

ingredients.name: ten to fifteen potatoes of equal size

steps: Cook the potatoes so that they do not burst. Also cook ten eggs hard, then place in cold water and clean them. Cut the potatoes and eggs into slices. Pour eight decilitres of sour cream over the top, place in the oven and bake.

title: Besamel (Béchamel Sauce)
description: A sauce made with cream, onion, and ham.

ingredients.name: half a Spanish onion (if for meat broth)

title: Besammel-felfújt (Béchamel Soufflé)
description: Prepared with melted butter, cream or milk, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: 40 grams ground and sifted sugar with vanilla
peach or raspberry syrup, wine or milk sauce

steps: In a pot, brown the fine flour in the melted butter
When the flour foams, gradually add cream or milk with constant stirring
Stir the whole mixture until it separates from the pot, then season lightly with salt
Cool on a plate
Beat the paste with ten egg yolks until foamy
Mix in sugar ground with vanilla
Finally fold in the stiffly beaten egg whites
Pour the mixture into a well-buttered mold and either steam for three-quarters of an hour or bake in a not too hot oven until a beautiful light yellow
Turn out onto a plate and pour peach or raspberry syrup, wine or milk sauce underneath

title: Birsalma párban (Quince Preserves in a Water Bath)
description: A fruit preserve made with quince, water, and sugar.
steps: Peel the quince and cut into slices two centimeters wide
Remove the seedy portion from the center and place in cold water
Boil the sugar with four deciliters of water until dissolved
Place the quince slices in the boiling syrup and stir continuously and very carefully with a silver spoon so the slices cook evenly
Cook until they can be pierced with a needle, but they must not become completely soft
Remove from heat and cool completely
Fill the jars, place them in a water bath (see recipe 961), and leave for at most three minutes

title: Birsalma sósborszeszben (Quince in Vinegared Spirits)
description: Prepared with quince or pear, sugar syrup, and sugar.

ingredients.name: strong vinegared spirits, same amount as the sugar syrup

steps: Peel the quince or quince-pear and cut into eight or more pieces depending on size.
Remove the seeds and place the quince in cold water.
Soften well in hot water and drain thoroughly.
Take 56 dekagrams quince to 42 dekagrams sugar and cook not too thickly.
Prepare the quince over three days as with other fruit, cooking the sugar quite thickly the last time.
Let cool and mix with an equal amount of strong vinegared spirits.
Pour over the quince already packed in glass jars.

title: Birsalma-fagylalt (Quince Ice Cream)
description: Prepared with quinces, sugar, and water.

ingredients.name: 4 large ripe quinces, peeled and sliced thinly

steps: Cook the quince slices with sugar and water in a preserving pan until the quince is completely softened
Cool it, then press through a clean, non-dense cloth
Mix with the juice of 2 lemons and cool completely
Pour into the ice cream mold and proceed as with other ice creams
For jelly made from the same mixture, use 1.5 decagrams of dissolved isinglass, strain through cloth and blotting paper as with all jellies
